### 1 — Scene
A mixed plate with a cooked rib section, two small browned patties or fritters, two fried sushi pieces, and one plain sushi piece.

### 2 — Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Cooked ribs, including visible bone
- Two browned patties/fritters; ingredients uncertain
- Two fried sushi pieces with an orange filling
- One plain sushi piece at the back  
No separate sauce or dressing is visible.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
The items cover approximately **33% of the plate**, leaving most of its lower and side areas exposed.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ribs, bone-in | 17% | 90 × 1.8 = 162 ml | 0.95 | 154 g | 230* | 354 kcal |
| Browned patties/fritters | 6% | 32 × 1.1 = 35 ml | 0.95 | 33 g | 220 | 73 kcal |
| Fried sushi, two pieces | 8% | 42 × 2.8 = 118 ml | 0.90 | 106 g | 240 | 254 kcal |
| Plain sushi, one piece | 2% | 11 × 2.0 = 22 ml | 0.90 | 20 g | 160 | 32 kcal |

*The rib energy density is expressed per bone-in plated weight, allowing for the non-edible bone. Frying oil is included in the fried foods’ energy densities.*

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **313 g and 713 kcal** is plausible for this partially covered plate. The rib composition and unidentified patties introduce the most uncertainty; roughly **600–850 kcal** is a reasonable range.
